title: PuTTYtel
subtitle: Simon Tatham, 1999- · the Win32 build, drawn through PRISM's own GDI
argsHint: PuTTY names its session on the command line; in the page there is no network, so it opens its window and reports that the host does not exist — which is the program's own path, not a stub.
_host: The Win32 GUI host: win32.c and win32-gui.c are compiled in, the surface is 32-bit BGRA rather than a palette, and the frame boundary is MsgWaitForMultipleObjects -- the one moment a GUI program with nothing to do comes back round.
_limits: No sockets: a browser has none to give, so a real session needs a WebSocket relay. What this shows is the window, the font and the terminal emulator.
_target: The target AND the variant. PuTTY's own default is `test-argv` -- the cheapest thing to run in Node -- and a page that took the default got a self-checking test with no window instead of the terminal.
